overview: DoorDash operates on-demand local commerce marketplaces -- the DoorDash Marketplace in the U.S., plus Wolt and Deliveroo internationally -- that connect merchants, consumers, and independent-contractor couriers ('Dashers') across more than 40 countries. It also runs a Commerce Platform (white-label delivery via 'Drive', online ordering, SevenRooms reservations/CRM, Bbot tableside ordering) that lets merchants build direct-to-consumer channels. Revenue is earned primarily as a take rate on Marketplace gross order value (merchant commissions and consumer delivery/service fees, net of Dasher payouts and promotions), supplemented by DashPass/Wolt+/Deliveroo Plus membership fees and a fast-growing advertising business.

business_model.summary: DoorDash monetizes a three-sided marketplace by taking a percentage of Marketplace Gross Order Value (GOV) -- merchant commissions plus consumer delivery/service fees, net of Dasher payouts, refunds and promotions ('Net Revenue Margin', ~13.6% of GOV in Q3 2026). Membership programs (DashPass, Wolt+, Deliveroo Plus; 35M+ members) and advertising (1B+ ARR run-rate, embedded in Marketplace revenue) add high-margin, recurring revenue on top of the core delivery take rate. The Commerce Platform (Drive white-label fulfillment, SevenRooms, Bbot, online ordering) is a smaller, largely transactional B2B revenue stream.

revenue_streams.name: DoorDash Marketplace (US restaurants/new verticals, commissions + consumer fees)
DashPass / Wolt+ / Deliveroo Plus membership fees
Commerce Platform (Drive, SevenRooms, Bbot, online ordering)

business_model.customer_type: Three-sided marketplace: B2C consumers, B2B/SMB and enterprise merchants (restaurants, grocers, convenience, retail, CPG advertisers), and independent-contractor Dashers
business_model.geographic_mix: United States ~78% of revenue, International ~22% (Q3 2026); international share jumped from ~15% a year earlier following the October 2025 Deliveroo acquisition, on top of the earlier Wolt (Finland-based) acquisition

competitive_position.market_position: Clear #1 in U.S. restaurant/local delivery with an estimated ~65-68% order share (Uber Eats ~23-25%, Grubhub ~8%, per third-party app/transaction data), and now a top global player internationally via Wolt and the newly-acquired Deliveroo (UK/Europe/Middle East/Asia/Australia)

moat_factors.description: More consumers attract more merchants and Dashers in a given market, improving selection, delivery speed and Dasher utilization, which is hard for a smaller #2/#3 player to replicate locally
Leading order density funds continued investment in routing, batching and demand-prediction algorithms that improve Dasher efficiency and unit economics relative to smaller competitors
DashPass/Wolt+/Deliveroo Plus membership (35M+ members) and merchant integrations (POS, Drive, SevenRooms, online ordering) create stickiness, though consumers still commonly multi-home across apps
Large, high-intent audience and first-party purchase data support a fast-growing ads business (1B+ ARR) that is difficult for smaller rivals to match
Scale of order and delivery data improves demand forecasting, fraud detection, and ad targeting over time

weaknesses: Thin historical margins and continued heavy investment (new global tech platform, AI tooling, international integration) keep Adjusted EBITDA margin on GOV in the low single digits
Consumer switching costs are modest -- multi-homing across delivery apps remains common and price/promotion sensitive
Structural reliance on an independent-contractor labor model that is under sustained legal and legislative challenge across jurisdictions
Self-operated grocery/convenience retail requires significant capital with uncertain unit economics at scale
Integration risk is stacking up (Deliveroo, SevenRooms, Symbiosys, Grubhub Campus Dining, and a pending ~$17B Instacart deal) across multiple concurrent acquisitions

growth_drivers: International expansion and cross-sell via Wolt (closed) and Deliveroo (closed Oct 2025) across 40+ countries

Pending ~$17B acquisition of Instacart (announced Oct 28, 2026) to add grocery/retail scale and cross-sell DashPass/Instacart+ memberships, subject to shareholder and antitrust approval (expected close late 2027/H1 2028)
Advertising monetization of merchant and CPG spend, including offsite ads via the Symbiosys acquisition
Grocery, convenience, and new-vertical expansion (alcohol, retail) beyond restaurant delivery, including self-operated retail locations
Commerce Platform growth: Drive white-label fulfillment, SevenRooms reservations/CRM, Bbot tableside ordering, online ordering for merchants' own channels
DashPass/Wolt+/Deliveroo Plus membership growth (35M+ members) increasing order frequency and reducing promotional spend
Multi-year investment in a new global technology platform and AI-native tooling intended to raise developer productivity and operational consistency
Acquisition of Grubhub's Campus Dining business (announced Sept 2026, ~$300M) extending into campuses, stadiums and hotels
Early-stage investment in autonomous/drone delivery technology

business.description: Uber Eats, Grubhub, Instacart, Amazon, Delivery Hero and local incumbents compete for merchants, consumers and Dashers; Uber sued DoorDash in California state court in Feb 2025 alleging anticompetitive practices
Simultaneous integration of Deliveroo, SevenRooms, Symbiosys, Grubhub Campus Dining and the pending Instacart deal raises execution risk and could divert management attention
Fixed-cost retail/fulfillment locations may not generate sufficient order volume to be viable, exposing the company to inventory shrinkage and new regulatory categories (food safety, permits, zoning)
Key KPIs (Total Orders, Marketplace GOV, Contribution Profit, Adjusted EBITDA) are tracked with internal, unaudited systems and could be inaccurate or subject to restatement

financial.description: The Instacart deal is to be funded partly by a $13.0B senior unsecured bridge loan commitment from JPMorgan, on top of existing $2.75B+ convertible notes, materially increasing debt and interest-rate exposure
Primary exposure to EUR, CAD, ILS and AUD is growing fast as international revenue mix rises post-Deliveroo/Wolt; FX translation swung comprehensive income by -$148M in the first nine months of 2026

financial.risk: History of GAAP losses / margin pressure
financial.description: Despite recent GAAP profitability, rising D&A from acquired intangibles (up 83% YoY for the first nine months of 2026) and stock-based compensation remain large costs

regulatory.description: Ongoing litigation and legislative activity in the U.S., EU (Platform Work Directive, in force since Dec 2024) and elsewhere could force reclassification of Dashers, Wolt courier partners, or Deliveroo riders as employees; Finland's Supreme Administrative Court ruled in May 2025 that Wolt courier partners are employees (DoorDash is seeking annulment)

The pending Instacart acquisition requires HSR clearance plus Canadian and Israeli antitrust approval given grocery-delivery overlap; DoorDash is also a defendant in Uber's California antitrust suit and faces ongoing competition-authority inquiries in several jurisdictions
Rules such as NYC's minimum earnings standard for food-delivery workers raise costs and have prompted fee increases that can dampen demand
EU Digital Services Act reporting obligations, data protection rules, and emerging AI regulation (EU and elsewhere) raise compliance costs and could constrain product deployment

macro.description: Demand is tied to employment, inflation, consumer confidence and discretionary spending; economic downturns or tariff/trade-driven cost inflation could reduce order volume
Higher-for-longer rates raise the cost of the new Instacart-related bridge financing and reduce interest income earned on cash balances
Conflicts in the Middle East and Ukraine have already affected regional operations and could disrupt markets where Wolt/Deliveroo operate

macro_factors.industry_outlook: On-demand local commerce (restaurant delivery, grocery, convenience, retail) continues to grow double-digits globally, though U.S. restaurant delivery penetration is maturing and growth is increasingly driven by grocery/retail expansion, advertising monetization, and international markets
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate -- discretionary consumer spending category, but subscription (DashPass-type) penetration and habitual usage dampen cyclicality versus pure discretionary retail; also exhibits weather- and seasonality-driven quarterly swings
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Rising -- previously low given net cash position, but the ~$13B Instacart bridge financing and existing convertible notes increase sensitivity to rates; interest income on ~$6-7B cash/investments is a modest tailwind when rates are elevated
key_input_costs: Grocery/retail cost of goods in self-operated locations

recent_developments.event: Completed acquisition of Deliveroo plc for ~$3.72B in cash, adding UK/European/Middle East/Asia-Pacific/Australia markets and recording $1.99B goodwill and $1.50B acquired intangibles
Finland's Supreme Administrative Court ruled Wolt courier partners are employees (though excluded from the Working Hours Act); DoorDash is seeking annulment
Reported record full-year 2025 results: revenue $13.72B, up 28% YoY from $10.72B in 2024
Recorded ~$51M in restructuring charges (nine months ended Sept 2026) tied to country-operations closures announced in Q1 2026
Amended and restated its revolving credit facility to $2.0B, maturing August 2031
Agreed to acquire Grubhub's Campus Dining business from Wonder for ~$300M and separately invested $125M in Wonder, extending into campus, stadium and hospitality dining
Completed reincorporation from Delaware to Nevada

Announced definitive agreement to acquire Instacart (Maplebear Inc.) for ~$17B equity value ($65.00/share cash, 0.3372 DASH shares, or a cash/stock mix, capped at 25% stock), backed by a $13.0B JPMorgan bridge loan; deal expected to close late 2027/H1 2028 pending Instacart shareholder and antitrust (US/Canada/Israel) approval

Reported Q3 2026 results: revenue $4.62B (+34% YoY) and diluted EPS $1.06, beating consensus (~$4.56B/$0.81-0.82); Marketplace GOV $33.9B (+36%); stock still fell on a softer-than-hoped Q4 profitability outlook and heavier planned investment, and several analysts trimmed price targets (e.g., Mizuho to $320 from $350, Oppenheimer to $280 from $350, MoffettNathanson to $239 from $277) while broadly maintaining Buy/Outperform ratings

items.notes: Implies continued ~25-30% YoY growth; assumes stable consumer demand and FX rates

Below Q3 2026's $1,060M; management guided Adjusted EBITDA as a % of GOV lower sequentially due to seasonal Dasher cost increases, annual insurance renewal, and continued investment in the technology platform and autonomy initiatives
Company guides on Marketplace GOV and Adjusted EBITDA rather than revenue directly; Net Revenue Margin has run ~13.6-13.8% of GOV in 2026

guidance.management_commentary: Management highlighted record Q3 2026 orders (993M, +28% YoY) and GOV growth (+36% YoY), attributing much of the acceleration to the Deliveroo acquisition and continued U.S. consumer growth. They reiterated a multi-year investment program in a new global technology platform and AI-native tooling intended to improve long-term developer productivity and operating consistency, acknowledging this carries near-term cost and will compress Q4 Adjusted EBITDA margin. The Instacart and Grubhub Campus Dining acquisitions were framed as extending DoorDash's reach into grocery and institutional dining, funded by cash on hand and new debt.

bull_case: Dominant U.S. market share (~65-68% of orders) built on network effects between merchants, consumers and Dashers that are difficult for Uber Eats or Grubhub to dislodge
Multiple, largely untapped growth vectors beyond core restaurant delivery: advertising (1B+ ARR), grocery/retail, Commerce Platform (Drive, SevenRooms), and international scale via Wolt/Deliveroo
Strong and growing free cash flow (~$1.9B over the first nine months of 2026) funds aggressive but disciplined M&A largely without heavy equity dilution
If completed, the Instacart acquisition would consolidate online grocery/delivery leadership and let DoorDash cross-sell DashPass/Instacart+ to a combined 35M+ paying membership base
Consumer membership programs (DashPass/Wolt+/Deliveroo Plus) and advertising create increasingly recurring, higher-margin revenue layered on top of transactional delivery fees
bear_case: Heavy, overlapping integration risk across Deliveroo, SevenRooms, Symbiosys, Grubhub Campus Dining and the pending ~$17B Instacart deal increases execution risk and could strain management bandwidth

The Instacart deal's ~$13B bridge financing materially increases leverage at a time analysts are already cutting price targets (Mizuho to $320, Oppenheimer to $280, MoffettNathanson to $239) on concerns about investment intensity and margin trajectory

Q4 2026 guidance implies a sequential decline in Adjusted EBITDA margin on GOV, and the stock sold off even after beating Q3 2026 consensus, reflecting investor concern about the pace and scale of spending

Gig-worker classification risk is structural and geographically broad: the Finland court ruling on Wolt couriers, the EU Platform Work Directive, and ongoing U.S. litigation could raise costs or force business-model changes in multiple markets simultaneously

Antitrust scrutiny is elevated on two fronts -- Uber's California lawsuit alleging anticompetitive conduct and the multi-jurisdiction (US/Canada/Israel) regulatory review required to close the Instacart acquisition -- creating event risk around a roughly 14-month-plus closing timeline
